summary: Israeli forces conducted airstrikes in Gaza, eliminating two Hamas operatives including a commander who infiltrated Israel on October 7. Saudi Arabia carried out airstrikes in Yemen targeting communication infrastructure and buildings in Saada, Taiz, and Hajjah provinces.

Iran's Red Crescent unveiled new rescue robots with plans for 100 units deployment. points: Iran's Red Crescent has unveiled new rescue robots designed to assist rescuers during emergencies and disaster response operations. The head of the Iranian Red Crescent stated that the number of these robots in the country will soon reach 100 units. These robotic systems represent a new capability for emergency response within Iran's domestic infrastructure. The announcement was made through official channels without specifying technical specifications or deployment timeline. (Source: @presstv/209062)

NATO Secretary General commented on Iran, stating that US attacks against Iran would be vital for European security. This statement reflects ongoing tensions regarding Iran's regional activities and nuclear program. The comment was reported by Iranian state media, indicating heightened rhetoric between Western officials and Iranian authorities. No specific details were provided about the context or timing of these alleged US attacks. (Source: @kianmeli1/92763)

Israeli airstrike in southern Gaza eliminated Hamas operative Mohammad Abdulaziz Mohammad Najjar, who infiltrated Israel on October 7 disguised as a journalist. The operation was conducted to remove an immediate threat posed by the individual who had been involved in terror activities against IDF forces and Israeli civilians. Prior to the strike, measures were taken to minimize civilian casualties including precise weaponry and aerial surveillance. IDF Southern Command forces remain deployed according to operational agreements. (Source: @New_security8200/204059)

Israeli airstrike in Gaza eliminated Hamas commander Amr Mahmoud Hamudi Rafi, a company commander in Hamas's military wing. The individual had been promoting terror infrastructure against IDF forces and Israeli civilians while attempting to rebuild Hamas capabilities in violation of ceasefire agreements. The targeted operation utilized precise weaponry and aerial observations to minimize civilian harm. IDF Southern Command continues operations to eliminate immediate threats. (Source: @New_security8200/204058)

Israeli Defense Minister identified the FlyDubai incident as a thwarted jihadist attack, crediting Israeli passengers who overpowered the assailant in the cockpit. The attacker's intent was reportedly to crash the aircraft killing all passengers. The minister emphasized that intelligence-based warnings should be taken seriously by both external enemies and internal critics. He reiterated that warnings complement rather than replace proactive operations against threats. (Source: @New_security8200/204047)

Israeli Supreme Court permitted publication of Lt. Col. Aryeh Amidror's name, linking him to October 7 intelligence failures. Amidror, former Gaza Division intelligence officer, dismissed detailed warnings about the impending Hamas attack as 'completely imaginary.' He was dismissed by IDF Chief of Staff in November but remained in service until recently after legal challenges. His father, retired General Yaakov Amidror, publicly opposed state commission investigations into October 7 without disclosing his son's involvement. (Source: @yediotnews25/135633)

sections.intelligence_notes: Lt. Col. Aryeh Amidror's dismissal of October 7 warnings as 'completely imaginary' reveals critical intelligence failures at senior levels. His father's public opposition to state commission investigations without disclosing personal involvement raises questions about transparency in accountability processes. Iranian Red Crescent robot deployment plans to 100 units suggest domestic emergency response modernization efforts.
